answer: A single karst checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a timber, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so anyone cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 464 aliases as a result costs 206 bonds held for 10 days each, plus the orchard attestations those aliases can never earn. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
